methodology: Two Sonnet sub-agents dispatched in parallel from mikkonumminen.dev master. Arm A given the task in plain language with explicit instructions not to invoke the built-in or read CLAUDE.md / .claude/skills/. Arm B given the verbatim /review built-in prompt (extracted from the Claude Code harness's system reminder for this session) and told to follow it exactly. Both arms produced a real code review markdown file in D:\tmp\. Token count from harness usage.total_tokens per sub-agent (same accounting convention as /mikko-skill-usage and /mikko-skill-calibration: input + output + cache_creation; cache_read excluded as cache hits paid upstream). N=1.

task.pr_summary: fix(skills): promote calibration arm-B into cost column + repeat repo banner across page breaks. 5 files, +225/-67.

builtins.name: review
builtins.label: /review
builtins.notes: Arm A scouted the codebase heavily (33 tool uses — reading scripts/, src/, docs/) before writing the review. Arm B followed the built-in's prescribed gh CLI recipe (gh pr view → gh pr diff → analyze) and produced the review in 3 tool uses. Both reviews land in the same quality band; arm A is more verbose with more nuanced low-severity findings, arm B is tighter and adheres to the prescribed section structure. The 63% saving comes almost entirely from arm A's exploratory scouting that the procedure short-circuits.

caveats: N=1 — single PR, single dispatch per arm. Re-running on a different PR (especially one with more files or a less-clear-cut diff) would land differently. The Spacepotatis portfolio average was 22% saved; this 63% result is the high end of the observed range so far.

Sub-agent execution is not identical to a user typing /review in their own session. The built-in resolves the slash command and pre-fills the prompt; in arm B that prompt was pasted into the sub-agent's brief by the operator. Behavior should match (same prompt text, same recipe), but the integration path differs.

Outcome equivalence verified at the artefact level only — both reviews exist, both cover the same PR, both reach similar verdicts. No deeper quality grading was applied. Arm A surfaces some additional low-severity observations arm B does not; whether that's a 'win' for arm A depends on whether the extra findings are signal or noise.
